Gate: Windows test collection and pane-data execution

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. Case: normal use - A Windows platform run reaches the pane-data test. The guarded import fixes collection, but `tests/test_pane_data.py:289` puts a literal newline in the held test command, which Forge executes with `shell=True` at `src/forge/fasttest.py:690`. Windows `cmd.exe` truncates a command at that newline, even inside quotes, as shown in this [cmd.exe reproduction](https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/issues/11259). Python therefore receives only the imports and never waits for the gate. The question, review-stop and lending cases cannot reliably keep their test run active, so the Windows proof can time out or pass without checking the intended wait.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - A task worker asks a question. This case writes the expected internal thread record directly instead of making the worker ask through `forge work`; the worker normally records the question at `src/forge/worker.py:420`. The proof can therefore pass if task workers stop recording their questions and the pane consequently omits them. It also depends on the current private record format, so a behavior-preserving change to that format would break the test.
